answer_1.quote: We create POWERTRANSFORMER, an encoder‑decoder model that rewrites sentences with a desired portrayal using agency connotation frames... Our approach jointly learns to reconstruct partially masked story sentences while also learning to paraphrase from an external corpus of paraphrases.
answer_1.outputs: Rewritten sentences with the targeted agency level (high, neutral, low) while preserving meaning.

answer_2.quote: We measure the accuracy of the change in agency... As a measure of meaning preservation, we use BERTScore F1... we measure fluency as perplexity (PPL)... we compute the fraction of output sentences that have a bigram that is repeated two or more times... Finally, we compute the fraction of generations that are unique...

answer_4.quote: We collect human judgments of the controllable revisions from several baselines and POWERTRANSFORMER... We design a head‑to‑head crowdsourcing task on Amazon Mechanical Turk where we ask raters to compare two outputs... workers were asked to judge whether either output is gibberish, then choose which revision has better targeted agency and which better preserves the meaning of the original sentence.
answer_4.guideline: Raters compare two model outputs for the same input and target agency, indicating which better achieves the desired agency, which better preserves meaning, and whether any output is gibberish.
